scenes.headline: Regular Expressions
scenes.subtitle: Pattern matching for messy text
scenes.narration: Regular expressions describe patterns in text, and they are essential for validating and pulling data out of messy logs and files.

scenes.headline: Common building blocks
items: Backslash-d matches a digit, backslash-w a word char
Plus and star repeat a pattern
Write patterns as raw strings like r'\d+'
scenes.narration: Character classes are the vocabulary of regex, where backslash-d matches any digit and backslash-w matches word characters. Quantifiers like plus and star control repetition, matching one-or-more or zero-or-more of the preceding pattern. Parentheses form a capture group, letting you pull out just the piece of the match you actually want. Finally, writing patterns as raw strings with an r prefix stops Python from mangling the backslashes.

scenes.headline: Extracting numbers from a log
scenes.code:
import re
line = 'INFO status=200 latency=45ms'
nums = re.findall(r'\d+', line)
print(nums)
scenes.narration: We import the re module and define a log line to search. The pattern backslash-d plus matches every run of one or more digits, and findall returns them all at once. The result is a list containing the status code and the latency, both as strings ready for further processing.

scenes.headline: A typical regex workflow
scenes.narration: You begin by writing a pattern that describes the text you are hunting for. You then run search to find the first match or findall to gather every match. From the results you read out any capture groups you defined, and finally you use those extracted values in your program.

scenes.headline: search versus match versus findall
scenes.narration: Search scans the whole string and returns the first match as an object, while match is stricter and only succeeds if the pattern sits at the very start of the string. Findall is different again, collecting every match into a plain list. Use search or match when you expect a single result, and findall when you want to extract them all.

scenes.headline: Capturing named groups
scenes.narration: Here the pattern uses a named group, marked by question mark P and a name in angle brackets, to label the digits after status equals. Search returns a match object, and we guard against no match with the if statement. Then we pull out the value by its name, which reads far more clearly than referring to a group by number.

scenes.text: Always write regex patterns as raw strings and test them on real data before trusting them.
scenes.narration: The takeaway is to always write patterns as raw strings and test them against real sample data, because untested regex is a frequent and sneaky source of bugs.
